title: Regularity of a generating sequence does not depend on the chosen generators of the ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the three regularity notions of a sequence depend only on the ideal generated, provided the sequence has the minimal possible length, and the proof is a 32-line argument built on the comparison of Koszul complexes. It first observes that a quasi-regular generating sequence of minimal length has free conormal module, which forces the given generators to form a basis and hence the maps from symmetric powers of the conormal module to be isomorphisms, so the given sequence is quasi-regular; then it compares the two Koszul complexes by a change-of-basis matrix, uses the invertibility of the determinant modulo the ideal and the annihilation of the cohomology by the ideal to upgrade an isomorphism after inverting the determinant to a quasi-isomorphism; finally the H1-regular and Koszul-regular cases are reduced to the quasi-regular one by the equivalence of the notions for such sequences. Each of the three steps uses one named statement of the chapter.
